This indicates a possible pathway where Neostigmine may contribute to the development or progression of Myasthenia Gravis, possibly through mechanisms related to neuromuscular function. The evidence is consistent across multiple paths, suggesting a potential role of Neostigmine in the pathophysiology of Myasthenia Gravis, though the exact mechanism remains unclear.
